description: Read a Unity text-serialized YAML asset through the shared LocusBridge Property Tree. Supported extensions are `.unity`, `.prefab`, `.asset`, `.mat`, `.anim`, `.controller`, `.overridecontroller`, `.playable`, and `.mask`. Importer and binary asset types such as `.fbx`, textures, and audio are outside this tool's coverage; when their imported Unity object still needs inspection, use `unity_execute` to load it with an Editor script. Start with the asset path, then pass returned child paths back to this tool until the relevant object, component, or field is verified; use unity_yaml_search only when the target path is unknown. `path` always contains both the Unity asset path and the optional internal property path, for example `Assets/Actions/LightNormalAttack1.asset/hitTrack/clips/4`. When Unity is connected, the tool reads the live Editor object graph first so unsaved values and hierarchy changes are visible; disk YAML is a strict fallback when the live target is unavailable. Every result begins with `[source: live Editor]` or `[source: disk YAML]`. Malformed live Editor responses end the tool call as errors. Every read attempts a compact expansion and returns all non-array descendants when the result stays within 4,000 characters, regardless of `depth`. Larger trees use the progressive outline: the selected node is level 0, direct children are level 1, and `depth` controls expansion. Reading a `.unity` asset root always returns only the GameObject hierarchy. `hierarchy_fields` selects the inline metadata shown on each GameObject line and defaults to Layer, Tag, and component types; component field values require a follow-up read of that GameObject or component path. Prefab Instance roots begin with an explicit source header, show effective values in their original hierarchy, and append `(override)` to overridden fields instead of exposing `m_Modification` for agent-side interpretation. Same-named sibling instances from one Prefab with identical component inventories are folded in the text outline and annotated with their total count; every individual indexed path remains addressable. `max_array_items` controls how many items each array exposes, including compact expansions, and defaults to four; every index remains directly addressable. A compound asset root lists every same-file Subasset in a separate addressable hierarchy. ObjectReferences use the same asset-qualified Subasset paths returned by this tree and never expose `#fileID` suffixes. The first same-file ObjectReference reached through serialized properties claims the child; arrays retain index order, shared/cyclic references keep their first canonical path, and non-serialized runtime fields never participate. Append the displayed hierarchy segments to the asset path to read that object. Loaded Scene roots expose their live GameObject hierarchy. Explicitly reading a GameObject or component with `Unity.Scenes.SubScene` appends the referenced authoring Scene hierarchy under `SubScene Authoring Hierarchy`; an open SubScene uses live Editor state and a closed SubScene uses its saved disk YAML, while every displayed child keeps the referenced Scene asset path for follow-up reads. Vectors, quaternions, colors, bounds, curves, and gradients are inline values that do not consume depth. Requested world-space transform values, Prefab source, active/static state, and RectTransform rects appear inline in hierarchy summaries; other derived context without a readable path, such as Parent, appears in separate sections. Continue by passing any returned child or Subasset path back to this tool. Same-file ObjectReferences are expanded at their first serialized C# field location. The tool never returns a whole raw YAML file or repeats asset metadata headers.

path.description: Asset-qualified Property Tree path such as `Assets/Actions/LightNormalAttack1.asset` or `Assets/Actions/LightNormalAttack1.asset/hitTrack/clips/4`. Use `~0` for `~` and `~1` for `/` inside one field-name segment.

depth.description: Number of child levels in the progressive outline when full non-array expansion would exceed 4,000 characters. Defaults to 2 and is hard-clamped to 4. Trees within 4,000 characters expand completely even when depth is explicitly provided; arrays remain capped at `max_array_items`.

max_array_items.description: Maximum number of elements expanded for each array, including when `path` points directly to an array. Defaults to 4; later indices remain directly addressable.

hierarchy_fields.description: Inline metadata to show on each GameObject line in Scene and Prefab hierarchy output. Select only fields required by the current task and keep the list minimal because every selected field expands every GameObject line. Use an empty array for names only. `world_position`, `world_rotation`, and `world_scale` are world-space values. `rect` is emitted only for GameObjects whose Transform is a RectTransform; ordinary Transform nodes omit it. Defaults to `layer`, `tag`, and `components`.
